subject: CloudMed MAP: performance closure & hosting comparison

Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudMed MAP: performance closure & hosting comparison

Hi Aiden —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our trapline, attaching an updated mutual action plan (MAP) that ties the evaluation pass/fail criteria to the close timeline you asked for. High level: we will validate throughput/latency/TTFT and concurrency behavior across three hosting modes (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and include isolation and autoscale observations.

Proposed evaluation plan (summary):
- Timeline: kickoff Mon 3/6, run automated workloads 3/7–3/9, buffer 3/10–3/11 for re-runs, decision by 3/13.
- Acceptance criteria (must meet at least two of three):
  - Median TTFT (time-to-first-token) <= 150ms at target concurrency (see below)
  - 95th percentile per-request latency growth < 25% when load increases 4x
  - Sustainable token throughput (tokens/sec) >= 18k tokens/sec for the baseline prompt mix
- Concurrency targets: baseline 16 concurrent sessions; scale tests at 32 and 64 concurrent sessions.
- Isolation checks: run noisy-neighbor synthetic workloads on co-tenants (for Hosted only) and measure latency variance.
- Autoscale behavior: observe ramp-up time to target concurrency, cold-starts, and pre-warm effectiveness.

Test harness we propose: standard Redwood perf harness v1.4 (attached), per-request token histogram capture, and end-to-end request/response diffs for quality validation. We will run the same harness in your dev account (Private), in a Redwood Dedicated pool provisioned for you, and against Hosted.

Requested from you:
- Confirmation that 3/6 kickoff works and you can provide a dev VPC endpoint and a small dataset (sanitized) by EOD 3/5.
- Any hard constraints for TTFT/throughput we should be aware of (e.g. internal SLAs).

I'll follow up with Rishi / Marissa to capture internal expected baselines so we can set realistic pass thresholds.

Best,
Sofia
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: CloudMed MAP: perf baselines / test harness notes

Sofia / team —

Quick tech note ahead of the kickoff. Test harness and a summary of our internal expectation below (these are from recent Redwood runs against a similar prompt mix):

Redwood internal baseline (representative):
- Hosted (multi-tenant):
  - Median TTFT: 120–210ms (depends on cold-starts & prefix cache)
  - 95th p latency (token-level): ~420–650ms under baseline concurrency (16)
  - Sustained throughput: 12k–20k tokens/sec for our L2 model on gpus with continuous batching
  - Observed variance under noisy neighbor test: latency sigma up to 30% (in the worst co-tenancy case)
- Dedicated (reserved pool):
  - Median TTFT: 80–120ms
  - 95th p latency: 220–350ms at 16 concurrency, scales linearly to 32 with <20% degradation
  - Sustained throughput: 18k–28k tokens/sec depending on sequence length
  - Autoscale: pre-warmed pools reduce cold-starts; ramp to 64 concurrency in ~45–90s depending on burst policy
- Private (customer infra):
  - Median TTFT: 70–150ms (hardware-dependent, network adds variability)
  - 95th p latency: highly dependent on infra, we see 200–500ms on well-provisioned clusters
  - Throughput: highly variable, recommend measuring tokens/sec per-GPU in their k8s environment before pass/fail

Recommended pass thresholds for CloudMed (conservative):
- TTFT median <= 160ms at 16 conc; <= 220ms at 64 conc
- 95th p latency growth < 30% between 16 -> 64 conc
- Sustained tokens/sec >= 15k in Hosted, >=18k in Dedicated, >=16k in Private (if hardware >= 4x A100)

Test harness notes:
- Use fixed seed prompts and a 70/30 ratio of short/long sequences to mimic CloudMed queries.
- Capture per-request micro-timings: client->router, router->worker, sample-gen time, network serialization.
- For autoscale, script a sawtooth load: 0 -> 16 -> 32 -> 64 -> back to 16 with 10s step hold to measure ramp and cooldown.

I'll stand up the Redwood Dedicated pool and pre-configure the harness. Marissa — can you schedule a 30m ops handoff with CloudMed on 3/6 after the DPA is signed?

-Rishi
Principal Performance Engineer

Date: Wed, 8 Mar 2028 17:25:00 -0700
Subject: CloudMed MAP: final test summary + next steps

Aiden / team —

Quick summary now that the three-mode runs have completed (see attached raw results + short screen capture of autoscale behavior). Notes and recommended next steps:

Summary of measured results (representative medians / 95th p where noted):
- Hosted (Redwood multi-tenant, baseline config):
  - Median TTFT: 145ms at 16 conc; TTFT increased to 225ms at 64 conc (95th p = 580ms)
  - Sustained throughput: ~14.8k tokens/sec sustained over 5m windows
  - Isolation: noisy-neighbor synthetic produced a 22% sigma increase in latency; variance reduced after we forced prefix cache warmup
  - Autoscale: ramp to 64 conc in ~110s (cold starts observed in first run)
- Dedicated (provisioned reserved pool for CloudMed):
  - Median TTFT: 95ms at 16 conc; 120ms at 64 conc (95th p = 310ms)
  - Sustained throughput: ~20.6k tokens/sec
  - Isolation: negligible (single-tenant), latency stable under burst
  - Autoscale: pre-warm policy achieved ramp in ~50s consistently
- Private (CloudMed k8s cluster 4x A100-equivalent):
  - Median TTFT: 85ms at 16 conc; 140ms at 64 conc (95th p = 420ms)
  - Sustained throughput: 17.9k tokens/sec (note: small degr when background jobs share GPUs)
  - Isolation: depends on node scheduling; we observed one test where co-located batch job spiked latency by +40%
  - Autoscale: Kubernetes HPA spin-up varied, observed 90–160s depending on node provisioning speed

Recommendation and path to close:
- Dedicated meets all MAP acceptance thresholds and gives the most predictable outcome.
- Private can meet thresholds but requires the managed-onprem addendum or CloudMed to adopt a strict node isolation policy (taints/tolerations and dedicated GPU nodes).
- Hosted is close on TTFT but shows the largest variance under noisy neighbors; acceptable if CloudMed accepts slightly higher tail latency and we include an initial 4-week ramp SLA credit in the SOW.

Next steps:
1) Procurement/DPA + sign SOW (Marissa to provide SOW draft on 3/9).
2) If Dedicated: provision start date 4/1, 90-day eval with metrics dashboard access.
3) If Private: Marissa to propose managed-onprem addendum pricing and integration plan.

I've attached the raw results and a short screen capture of autoscale behavior to help procurement/CTO evaluate. Happy to jump on a 20m call Fri 3/10 to walk through the results with your ops team.

Thanks,
Sofia
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
